prerequisites: It is strongly recommended to have passed, or at least taken, the courses "Elasticity and Strength of Materials" I and II.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and capabilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
Knowledge and capabilities for the design, analysis and calculation of mechanisms and mechanical systems.
Capacity for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Capacity to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Capacity for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Structures
Actions in Building
Supports and Connections in Structures
Resolution of Articulated Structures by Equilibrium Methods and Energy Methods
Translational and Intranslational Reticular Structures and their Resolution by Moment Distribution Methods
Matrix Calculation of Structures: Theory and Practical Resolution of Structures
BLOCK A: INTRODUCTION TO STRUCTURES
Topic 1.- Introduction to Structural Calculation
Topic 2.- Actions in building
Topic 3.- Supports and connections in structures
BLOCK B: ARTICULATED STRUCTURES
Topic 4.- Articulated structures. Isostatic trusses
Topic 5.- Articulated structures. Hyperstatic trusses
Topic 6.- Energy theorems
BLOCK C: RETICULAR STRUCTURES
Topic 7.- Introduction to the study of reticular structures
Topic 8.- Calculation of intranslational reticular structures
Topic 9.- Calculation of translational reticular structures
Topic 10.- Moment distribution method
BLOCK D: INTRODUCTION TO MATRIX CALCULATION
Topic 11.- Generalities of Matrix Calculation
Topic 12.- The direct stiffness method
Topic 13.- Matrix analysis of structures on computer
BLOCK E: INFLUENCE LINES
Topic 14.- Influence lines in isostatic beams
Practice 1 (Block A): Calculation of actions on industrial building
Practice 2 (Block B): Calculation of articulated structure using spreadsheet
Practice 3 (Block C): Calculation of reticular structure using various methods
Practice 4 (Block D): Calculation of structures using matrix analysis
Practice 5 (Block E): Influence lines of isostatic beam under a train of loads
teaching_methods: Practical sessions (in small groups, computer labs)
Field visits to ongoing works and permanent installations
Collective tutorials (for specific doubts and practical problem review)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Theoretical Exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises

assessment_rules: To pass the course, it is necessary to pass theory (exam) and practicals (practice reports) separately. In the theoretical exam, it will be necessary to score in both theoretical and operational contents of the subject, having a grade greater than zero in each of these parts. The weight of theoretical contents in the exam will be 30% compared to 70% for operational contents (problems).
